253: class FindDataSourceTable(sparkSession: SparkSession) extends Rule[LogicalPlan] {
254:   private def readDataSourceTable(
255:       table: CatalogTable, extraOptions: CaseInsensitiveStringMap): LogicalPlan = {
256:     val qualifiedTableName =
257:       QualifiedTableName(table.identifier.catalog.get, table.database, table.identifier.table)
258:     val catalog = sparkSession.sessionState.catalog
259:     val dsOptions = DataSourceUtils.generateDatasourceOptions(extraOptions, table)
260:     val readFileSourceTableCacheIgnoreOptions =
261:       SQLConf.get.getConf(SQLConf.READ_FILE_SOURCE_TABLE_CACHE_IGNORE_OPTIONS)
262:     catalog.getCachedTable(qualifiedTableName) match {
263:       case null =>
264:         val dataSource =
265:           DataSource(
266:             sparkSession,
267:             // In older version(prior to 2.1) of Spark, the table schema can be empty and should be
268:             // inferred at runtime. We should still support it.
269:             userSpecifiedSchema = if (table.schema.isEmpty) None else Some(table.schema),
270:             partitionColumns = table.partitionColumnNames,
271:             bucketSpec = table.bucketSpec,
272:             className = table.provider.get,
273:             options = dsOptions,
274:             catalogTable = Some(table))
275:         val plan = LogicalRelation(dataSource.resolveRelation(checkFilesExist = false), table)
276:         catalog.cacheTable(qualifiedTableName, plan)
277:         plan

49: case class CreateDataSourceTableCommand(table: CatalogTable, ignoreIfExists: Boolean)
50:   extends LeafRunnableCommand {
51: 
52:   override def run(sparkSession: SparkSession): Seq[Row] = {
53:     assert(!table.isViewLike)
54:     assert(table.provider.isDefined)
55: 
56:     val sessionState = sparkSession.sessionState
57:     if (sessionState.catalog.tableExists(table.identifier)) {
58:       if (ignoreIfExists) {
59:         return Seq.empty[Row]
60:       } else {
61:         throw QueryCompilationErrors.tableAlreadyExistsError(table.identifier.unquotedString)
62:       }
63:     }
64: 
65:     // Create the relation to validate the arguments before writing the metadata to the metastore,
66:     // and infer the table schema and partition if users didn't specify schema in CREATE TABLE.
67:     val pathOption = table.storage.locationUri.map("path" -> CatalogUtils.URIToString(_))
68:     // Fill in some default table options from the session conf
69:     val tableWithDefaultOptions = table.copy(
70:       identifier = table.identifier.copy(
71:         database = Some(
72:           table.identifier.database.getOrElse(sessionState.catalog.getCurrentDatabase))),
73:       tracksPartitionsInCatalog = sessionState.conf.manageFilesourcePartitions)
74:     val dataSource: BaseRelation =
75:       DataSource(
76:         sparkSession = sparkSession,
77:         userSpecifiedSchema = if (table.schema.isEmpty) None else Some(table.schema),
78:         partitionColumns = table.partitionColumnNames,
79:         className = table.provider.get,
80:         bucketSpec = table.bucketSpec,
81:         options = table.storage.properties ++ pathOption,
82:         // As discussed in SPARK-19583, we don't check if the location is existed
83:         catalogTable = Some(tableWithDefaultOptions))
84:         .resolveRelation(checkFilesExist = false,
85:           forceNullable = !sessionState.conf.getConf(SQLConf.FILE_SOURCE_INSERT_ENFORCE_NOT_NULL))
86: 
87:     val partitionColumnNames = if (table.schema.nonEmpty) {
88:       table.partitionColumnNames
89:     } else {
90:       // This is guaranteed in `PreprocessDDL`.
91:       assert(table.partitionColumnNames.isEmpty)
92:       dataSource match {
93:         case r: HadoopFsRelation => r.partitionSchema.fieldNames.toImmutableArraySeq
94:         case _ => Nil
95:       }
96:     }
97: 
98:     val newTable = dataSource match {
99:       // Since Spark 2.1, we store the inferred schema of data source in metastore, to avoid
100:       // inferring the schema again at read path. However if the data source has overlapped columns
101:       // between data and partition schema, we can't store it in metastore as it breaks the
102:       // assumption of table schema. Here we fallback to the behavior of Spark prior to 2.1, store
103:       // empty schema in metastore and infer it at runtime. Note that this also means the new
104:       // scalable partitioning handling feature(introduced at Spark 2.1) is disabled in this case.
105:       case r: HadoopFsRelation if r.overlappedPartCols.nonEmpty =>
106:         logWarning("It is not recommended to create a table with overlapped data and partition " +
107:           "columns, as Spark cannot store a valid table schema and has to infer it at runtime, " +
108:           "which hurts performance. Please check your data files and remove the partition " +
109:           "columns in it.")
110:         table.copy(schema = new StructType(), partitionColumnNames = Nil)
111: 
112:       case _ =>
113:         table.copy(
114:           schema = dataSource.schema,
115:           partitionColumnNames = partitionColumnNames,
116:           // If metastore partition management for file source tables is enabled, we start off with
117:           // partition provider hive, but no partitions in the metastore. The user has to call
118:           // `msck repair table` to populate the table partitions.
119:           tracksPartitionsInCatalog = partitionColumnNames.nonEmpty &&
120:             sessionState.conf.manageFilesourcePartitions)
121: 
122:     }
123: 
124:     sessionState.catalog.createTable(newTable, ignoreIfExists)
125: 
126:     Seq.empty[Row]
